newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power holds steady in thin demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power holds steady in thin demand.

text.p: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity was trading mostly steady with thin demand amidst the autumn temperatures, brokers and marketers said.

New outages in the area, including Wisconsin Electric Power taking its 485 megawatt Point Beach nuclear unit 2 off line for 42 days for scheduled maintenance, were reported to have had little impact on prices.
On-peak, non-firm next day power for Tuesday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was pegged in the 15.00-15.50 range from $14.50-16.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was pegged steady in the $8.00-9.00 range.
On-peak non-firm prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Tuesday delivery were discussed at $17.50-18.50 from $17.00-18.00 last week.
Off-peak non-firm MAIN power was said to be steady in the $11.00-12.50 range.
November MAIN electricity was also pegged steady in the $19.00-19.50 range for delivery of a peak 16-hour block through the five business days of the week.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak non-firm power prices for Tuesday were said to be at $16.00-18.50 from $17.00-18.00 last week.
Off peak non-firm ECAR was said to be steady at $12.00-13.50.
November ECAR was said to be discussed relatively steady near $17.00-18.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak non-firm power in the south of the region was assessed at $17.00-19.00 from near $17.30 last week, the sources said.
November SPP was discussed at $19.50-20.50 from near $20.50 last week, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
